newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Dorgan postpones meeting on Canada wheat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Dorgan postpones meeting on Canada wheat.

text.p: North Dakota Senator Byron Dorgan has postponed a late day meeting with top Clinton Administration agriculture and trade officials about Canada wheat shipments, a spokesman for the senator said Wednesday.
The spokesman said Dorgan had to reschedule the meeting because he was called to the White House for budget talks. A new date has not been set, but it will likely be next week, the aide said.

Dorgan and fellow North Dakota Senator Kent Conrad, both Democrats, were slated to meet privately with Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman and U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky at 1730 EDT/2130 GMT.

The two senators earlier Wednesday demanded "immediate U.S. action" to stop Canada from exceeding the voluntary wheat export limits agreed upon two years ago. The pair planned to ask Barshefsky to cut off any further wheat or durum shipments from Canada this year, the spokesman said.
